observations: Single solar panel with a silver aluminum frame.
The panel has 96 cells arranged in an 8x12 grid.
The surface appears dusty or slightly soiled, consistent with being used.
No brand name, logo, or model number is visible on the front of the panel.
A watermark 'YOUNG MIRACLE GLOBAL LINK' is visible across the center.
The back of the panel, where the specification label is usually located, is not shown.

claims.evidence: No brand markings are visible in photo 0; the manufacturer's label on the back is missing.
The power rating is typically found on the rear nameplate, which is not pictured.
Counting the cells in photo 0 confirms an 8x12 grid, totaling 96 cells.

risks.risk: The panel may not be the claimed brand or wattage.
risks.proof: A clear photo of the specification label (nameplate) on the back of the panel.
risks.if_unproven: priced as a generic used 250W panel

risks.risk: The panel may have low output due to degradation or internal micro-cracks.
risks.proof: A video showing a multimeter test of Open Circuit Voltage (Voc) and Short Circuit Current (Isc) in full sun.
risks.if_unproven: priced as a non-functional or heavily degraded unit

risks.risk: Potential glass cracks or frame damage not visible in low-resolution photo.
risks.proof: Close-up photos of the glass surface and the four corners of the frame.
risks.if_unproven: priced as having minor physical defects

proof_requests: Photo of the manufacturer's specification label on the back of the panel.
Close-up photos of the glass surface to check for cracks.
Video of a multimeter test showing voltage and amperage in direct sunlight.
response.reason: The critical information required to value the item—the brand and the rated wattage—is only found on the rear label, which is not provided. Without this, the item cannot be distinguished from much lower-value generic panels.
